ambient_events: Something unspeakable gurgles down the floor drain and isn't discussed.
A regular knocks the bar twice; the bartender pours without looking.
The single TV shows horse racing from a track that no longer exists.
A fly, impossibly, in this cold, orbits the room in slow figure-eights.
A dull thud carries through from the back room, followed by a short, appreciative silence.
A foam-wrapped slag rolls out from under a stool; someone toes it back north without looking.
description: The kind of bar that doesn't need a name over the door because if you're here, you already knew where you were going. SUMP is scratched into the paint anyway. It's one narrow room, a plank bar, and a floor that slopes toward a literal drain in the center, hence the name and hence the smell. It sells drinks, cheap and strong and served without conversation, and it does that mostly as a formality: the Sump's real trade is through the doorway north, in the back room, where the chalk ring is. That's the pit: half gym and half grudge match, where the regulars throw foam-wrapped orbs at each other until only one is left standing. It runs the game the whole basin plays, the one a made-for-TV picture on Sub-Channel 2½ swears blind was invented right here. The regulars out front are fixtures, welded to their stools by decades of gravity and grievance, and every last one of them has taken a slag to the face and asked for another round.

window.description: A full-height pane onto the street, kept just clean enough to trade through. Whatever the weather is doing out there, it's doing it in plain view.
window.name: the shopfront window
